Vs.

full_judgment: Thus, even where a witness has been declared hostile, cross-examined by the prosecution and his evidence given in the Committing Court has been put in under section 288 Cr.P.C. by the prosecution, the Court in spite of such fact may take into consideration the evidence given by the witness at the trial. In this connection a reference may also be made to the decision in the case of Shuruj Mia & others vs. The Crown (1950) 2 DLR 114 wherein it has been observed that there is no rule is law the it the evidence of a witness who has been declared as hostile by the prosecution must be rejected, either in whole or in part, or that it must be rejected so far as it favours the party calling the witness or so far as it favours the opposite party. Where a witness contradicts or retracts in the Court of Sessions his earlier statement made in the Inquiring Court the Court has to determine which is the true version and has also to determine the veracity of the witness and act upon it. A reference may also be made to the decision in the case of Chhota Gada & others Vs. The State, (1963) 15 D.L.R. 517 wherein it has been held that while considering the questions of admission of evidence under section 288 Cr.P.C. application of section 145 of the Evidence Act is indispensable and that only such portion of the evidence given in the Inquiring Court can be treated as substantive evidence to which the attention of the witness is drawn and no other. In assessing the evidentiary value of the deposition of a witness who has been declared hostile by the prosecution and whose evidence given in the Committing Court has been put in by the prosecution under section 288 Cr.P.C. the entire evidence given by the witness in the trial Court and the portion of the evidence given by him in the Committing Court to which his attention has been drawn at the time of trial is for consideration of the Court for what it is worth. The Court is to reach its own conclusions as to the value to be attached to the statements which the witness has made in the Committing Court and the trial Court.
